main_statement.latex: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\longrightarrow(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings. Then $e(R)\leq e(S)$. There is no restriction on the dimensions, the residue fields, or the characteristics of the rings.
main_statement.paraphrase: Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity never decreases along a flat local map of Noetherian local rings (Lech 1960 conjecture), in full generality. Proof: reduce to complete, equidimensional, domain source, algebraically closed target residue field; build R -> T -> S=T/J with e(T)=e(R) and the complex F = P (x) K(x;T) (IMW2022); a new uniform lower bound for H_0 of complexes with deep entries over any ring with an abstract length (Thm 2.1, blowup + Eisenbud-Schreyer supernatural bundle with roots at critical points of prod(x+i)) gives e_HK(J+(x),T) >= e(T) in char p (then Ma's identity gives e(S)), a normalized-perfectoid-length version in mixed char (Heitmann BS replaces Frobenius, prime-filtration upper bound), and char 0 by Artin approximation + specialization.

comparator.statement: for every complete (IsAdicComplete m) Noetherian local domain D of char p and every IsShortComplex F (cochain complex of finite free D-modules in degrees -dim D..0, finite-length homology, H^0 != 0): all Frobenius-twisted homology has finite length, duttaSequence converges to duttaMultiplicity, and multiplicity D <= duttaMultiplicity D p F.
comparator.model: multiplicity = limUnder of d! l(A/m^N)/N^d; dimension = ringKrullDim.toNat; Frobenius complex via ModuleCat.extendScalars (iterateFrobenius); cochain indexing (homological degree i = cochain degree -i)

main_statement.match_check: Comparator = paper's Corollary 4.4 (cor:dutta-domain, sections/charp.tex:193-201) plus existence of the Dutta limit (which the paper cites from IMW2022 4.17). Definitions match Def 4.3 (charp.tex:148-169) up to cochain sign convention; shortEuler sums over the d+1 nonzero degrees, which is all of them by `bounded`. Tendsto clause prevents vacuity from limUnder junk values. No loophole found at text level.
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: the Dutta corollary (and in fact for all complete char-p local rings, dutta_complete_charp drops IsDomain), hence the full uniform complex estimate Thm 2.1 in the generality of an abstract TorsionLength (complex_estimate_basis), the char-p normalized length on the perfection, Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem, coefficient fields, minimal reductions, residue extension, prime filtrations. NOT formalized: Lech's conjecture itself in any characteristic (no Cohen factorization, no Ma HK identity, no mixed-char perfectoid lengths/Heitmann, no char-0 Artin approximation). lean/docs/194.md: 'The paper's full flat-local result in arbitrary characteristic is outside it.'
main_statement.note_for_comparator: Headline != comparator target (pilot lesson 1). The comparator certifies the key new device (I08) in the char-p perfection instance only; the mixed-char and char-0 legs and the char-p Lech assembly (I32-I34) rest on the paper.

A.label: A1

evidence.quote: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)\longrightarrow(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings. Then $e(R)\leq e(S)$.

A.note: Universal inequality over all flat local maps. Not A3: the constant 1 is the conjectured one but no sharpness/rate is claimed. The key lemma Thm 2.1 is A3-style (explicit O_h(1/s) error, uniform constant A_h).

B.label: B1

evidence.quote: We prove Lech's multiplicity conjecture ... The result holds in arbitrary dimension, with no restrictions on the residue fields or characteristics.

B.note: Resolves Lech 1960 fully. Corollary: IMW2022 Conjecture 8.1 (Dutta multiplicity >= e(R)) for complete char-p local domains (paper) / all complete char-p local rings (Lean). Uses Ma's reductions and HK identity and IMW's complex construction, but those are tools, not partial cases of the conjecture.

primary_evidence.quote: Tensoring the resulting complex with a suitable vector bundle places its global hyperhomology in degree zero, modulo length zero, and hence gives a nonnegative Euler characteristic.

proof_architecture.claim: Reductions: complete, dim R = dim S > 0, R a domain, residue field of S algebraically closed (Nagata localization at a fibre prime, prime filtration additivity, residue extension).

Uniform complex estimate (Thm 2.1) for any ring C and abstract length lambda: blowup Y of I, twisted complex G = O(-is)^{b_i}, supernatural bundle V with roots ~ s*(critical points of prod(x+i)); chi(G(x)V) >= 0, Euler comparison chi(F_Y)=lambda H_0(F), equal layer sums (h-1)! s^h isolate b_0.

Length inputs: char p - Faltings normalized length on D_perf computes e_HK and makes parameter Koszul homology negligible (Roberts); mixed char - CLMST perfectoid length gives lambda(C/HC) <= e(H,D) with equality on parameter ideals.
Factorization R -> T -> S=T/J (Cohen factorization of A -> S, T=R(x)_A U), e(T)=e(R), J perfect, F = P (x) K(x;T) of length h, rank-0 alternating, contractible off the closed point.
Char p: Frobenius makes entries deep (s=q-c); per component e_HK(HD,D) >= e(D); HK associativity e_HK(J+(x),T) >= e(T); Ma's identity e_HK(J+(x),T)=e(S).
Corollary: Dutta multiplicity >= e(R) for short complexes over complete char-p domains (IMW Conj 8.1 case) - the Lean comparator.

Mixed char: p-power roots of parameters + Heitmann BS give deep entries in finite normal D of rank r; lower bound lambda/r >= e(B)(1-h/q)^h(1-K/(q-h)); prime-filtration upper bound after N-limit; q-limit; sum over components with coefficient 1 by generic regularity.

lean_structure.core_vs_implementation: Extractor v3 (data/items/194_lean.json). 688/3499 DAG decls flagged plumbing. Upstream closure of complex_estimate_basis = 2679 (76.6%; dominated share 0.70): the blowup/supernatural-bundle machinery implemented with explicit Cech complexes on chart rings (ReesRoot 286, ProductSourceCover 246, RootInvariants 124, ProjectiveRoot 110, AlternatingCech 103, FiniteModuleCech 77, SourceGraded 73, ...). The char-p normalized length construction (exists_length_with_module_limit) is 687 decls (19.6%), including Roberts' theorem and the SeparableOrder route. The numerical root choice (NumericalSupport: H, rho, roundedRoot, Riemann error) is only ~38 decls (1.1%). Reductions/Dutta assembly (prime filtration, residue extension, minimal complexes, minimal reductions) are each < 5%. Nearly all of the 'mathematical core' is the I08 package; within it, Eisenbud-Schreyer bundle re-implementation (transfer) is the largest block.
route_differences_from_paper: Lean proves the Dutta bound for every complete Noetherian local ring of char p (dutta_complete_charp, no IsDomain); the comparator only asks for domains. The paper's own proof (charp.tex:255-311) already handles non-domains via prime filtration, so this is the IMW Conj 8.1 in char p in full, not just the domain case.

No Cohen-Gabber: the char-p length is built over the separable order {x in D separable over K} (FrobeniusIntermediatePowerMap.lean:153-273) instead of a generically separable normalization (Kurano-Shimomoto).
Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem is re-proved in Lean via a conductor bound (RobertsSeparable.lean:50-155), not imported.

Blowup and the Eisenbud-Schreyer bundle are encoded as explicit Cech complexes over chart rings and ordered-root (RootUlrich) bases, not as schemes/sheaves; the core estimate needs only DirectSumZero, not the filtered-colimit axiom (ComplexEstimate.lean:92).
Lean's char-p setup requires perfect and infinite residue field at the domain stage (DuttaMinimalEstimate.lean:17-18), reached via residueExtension to an algebraically closed residue field.

correctness_audit.verdict: Extraordinary claim (Lech 1960, open in dim >= 4 even in equal characteristic until this release). The core Section 2 argument was checked line by line at the level of signs, degrees and root-position inequalities and is internally consistent; it is also machine-checked (pending compile) in its char-p instance via the Dutta comparator, which contains the full Theorem 2.1 for an abstract TorsionLength. The char-p Lech assembly (Cohen factorization + Ma HK identity) is short and follows Ma 2017's own reduction, so it is credible given Theorem 2.1. The mixed-char and char-0 legs are unformalized and rest on precise forms of cited results (Heitmann-Ma Prop 2.8, CLMST Cor 4.0.18, Ma Sec 5) that were not verified from full texts.

Mixed characteristic relies on HeitmannMa Prop 2.8 giving genuine membership b D subset (z)^{q-h} D in a finite extension. Heitmann-Ma's main results are phrased for extended plus closure (c^{1/p^e} x in (I,p^n)R^+), which is an 'almost' statement; if Prop 2.8 is only of that form, eq. (mixed-deep-entries) needs an almost-version of Theorem 2.1 (plausibly repairable via CLMST Prop 4.0.10 almost-invariance, but not done in the paper). Highest-priority check.

Mixed characteristic also needs lambda_infty(C/HC) <= e(H,D) for all d-primary H (CLMST Def 4.0.8 / Cor 4.0.18) and Koszul almost-vanishing for every s.o.p. of D (Cor 4.0.4 with n=0); stated precisely but not verified from the full text.

Char-0 leg follows Ma Section 5; the one-sided certificate is new detail. Point to check: Theorem charzero applies Lemma reduction then Lemma finite-free, which needs equal dimensions (provided), and the specialized map must be flat local of char-p rings (finite free + local: yes).

Section 2 Euler comparison (lem:complex-euler-comparison) is intricate (three towers, eventual images modulo length zero, non-Noetherian C); only spot-checked by hand. The Lean char-p instance covers it if the build succeeds.

Only the Dutta corollary is formalized; Lech's conjecture itself (even char p) has no Lean statement. If the comparator build fails, everything reduces to a 3.2k-line unrefereed paper whose key section is nonetheless short and checkable.
